answer: A stake-bonded reputation vine works like this: each agent must lock a deposit that grows along its history of attested work, so a new fake identity starts with nothing. An atlas of past attestations lets peers check whether an identity has real, costly history before trusting it. Creating a thousand sock puppets then means funding a thousand deposits and a thousand believable histories, while a single honest agent pays once - the dune of fake identities collapses under its own cost because each copy must pay full price for trust it has not earned.
